liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dondante** (3 reviews): The performance was described as soaring and majestic, though less effective than older versions; The track was featured as a soaring, majestic highlight of the three-hour show [7][13][16]
- **A Quick One$** (2 reviews): This cover of a Who song was highlighted as a particularly strong new addition; This cover of a Who song was singled out as a killer new addition [7][13]
- **Run Thru** (2 reviews): The track was characterized as facemelting during the three-hour set; The performance was described as facemelting, contributing to the overall Jacket-y goodness [7][13]

## Setlist highlights

- **Older Guys**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **Head Held High**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **Interlude**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **A Quick One$**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **Loving Cup**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **Easy Morning Rebel Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **Attitude**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **Evelyn Is Not Real**: back after 55 archived shows (987 days) [17]

## The recordings

- **mmj2006-06-16.km140.flac24** (recommended): source not stated; 33 songs; 182 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [1]
- **mmj2006-06-16.km140.flac16**: source not stated; 33 songs; 182 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: The recording quality is noted as smooth and not bad overall [8]
- **MMJ2006-06-16..4011s**: source not stated; 31 songs; 194 min; rated 4.56/5 by 9 [3]. Said about its sound: The audio is described as smooth, with covers successfully made into their own [9]
- **mmj2006-06-16.mk4**: source not stated; 31 songs; 189 min [4]

## Around the show

- Jim James's vocal intensity caused the audience to swell and erupt in rapture [5]
- Patrick Hallahan drummed intensely, driving the band's energy during the most intense moment [10]
- Festival attendees who disliked the band gravitated to the set as the music swelled [11]
- The band played nearly two hours past their scheduled set end time [11]
- Jim James and the band communicated stories to the audience rather than just playing songs [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **mmj2006-06-16.km140.flac24**: taped by Ed; transferred by Ed; source: Neumann AK40/LC3/KM100 (DIN) > Lunatec V3 > Edirol R4 (24/96) [1]. Also: KC Guetig played percussion and Mike DeSalvo played guitar for this specific recording; The show was recorded with the band's permission in a taper-friendly environment [1]
- **mmj2006-06-16.km140.flac16**: taped by Ed; transferred by Ed; source: Neumann AK40/LC3/KM100 > Lunatec V3 > Edirol R4 [2]
- **MMJ2006-06-16..4011s**: taped by Mark Lynn; transferred by Mark Lynn; source: DPA(B&K) 4011s->Luminous Monarchs [3]
- **mmj2006-06-16.mk4**: taped by Brent Stober; transferred by Brent Stober; source: Schoeps mk4 (DIN) > kc5 > cmc6 > Lunatec V3 > Sony D-8 @ 16/44.1 [4]
